invention.ref: Polished obsidian mirrors are attested in Neolithic Anatolia around 6000 BCE; this is an archaeological benchmark, not an invention date
invention.ref_zh: 约公元前6000年安纳托利亚已有磨光黑曜石镜；这是考古见证年代，并非确定的发明年份

埃及阿拜多斯（约前1800—1600年的青铜镜实物）
locations.place_label_en: Abydos, Egypt (bronze mirror dated ca. 1800–1600 BCE)

sources.title: Mirrors — Pitt Rivers Museum, University of Oxford
Mirror E9211, Abydos, 1800–1600 BCE — Penn Museum

notes: 人造镜并无可确认的单一发明者。约前6000年是博物馆对早期黑曜石镜的概括年代，加泰土丘地点代表考古发现，不是已证实的唯一发源地。阿拜多斯节点仅示意前1800—1600年青铜镜的实物记录，以前1700年作为区间中点，不表示青铜镜当时才出现，也不表示两地存在直接传播路线。
notes_en: No single inventor is established. The ca. 6000 BCE benchmark summarizes early obsidian mirrors; Çatalhöyük marks an archaeological findspot, not a proven exclusive birthplace. The Abydos marker uses 1700 BCE as the midpoint of a surviving bronze mirror’s 1800–1600 BCE range, not the first bronze mirror or evidence of direct transmission.
summary_zh: 镜子先于玻璃镜存在。约公元前6000年，安纳托利亚已有磨光黑曜石镜；埃及也留下了青铜镜实物。早期地点记录的是考古见证，无法据此确定唯一发明者。
summary_en: Mirrors predate glass mirrors: polished obsidian examples survive from Neolithic Anatolia around 6000 BCE, and bronze examples from Egypt. These finds do not establish a single inventor.
